turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?

Doctor: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today? Patient: I’ve just been feeling oddly detached from things around me, and my family interactions haven’t been holding my interest. Lately I’ve also found myself craving chocolate pudding and potato chips, and I’ve gained about 10 kilograms without really planning it.
Doctor: How long have you been noticing these feelings of detachment, loss of interest, and the changes in your eating habits?
Patient: It’s been about six months now—my detachment and lack of interest have been going on since then, and the food cravings and weight gain have followed along with it.
Doctor: Over the past six months, have you noticed any changes in your sleep—such as sleeping much more than usual, feeling rested, or having trouble staying asleep?
Patient: I don’t really pay attention to my sleep much—I mostly just feel apathetic about everything, and I wouldn’t say I’ve been sleeping dramatically more or less.
Doctor: Have you been feeling consistently low or sad most of the day, or would you describe your mood as more “flat” or “numb” rather than sad?

Patient: Mostly it feels flat and numb rather than sad, like I’m just going through things without much feeling. I can be careless about what I say or do, and I’ve noticed it’s gotten worse over the same six months.
Doctor: Have you had any trouble concentrating, making decisions, or noticing that your thinking feels “slowed” or “fuzzy” during this time?

Patient: I haven’t really focused on it, but I guess my thinking feels slower and I have trouble deciding things. I also don’t seem to concentrate well, and I tend to comment without thinking things through.
Doctor: Have you experienced any unusual thoughts, beliefs, or perceptions—such as hearing voices, seeing things that aren’t there, or feeling that people are talking about you?
Patient: I haven’t noticed hearing voices or seeing anything others don’t, and I don’t feel like people are talking about me—mostly I just go numb and do or say things without really checking myself.
Doctor: Have you had any thoughts of harming yourself or wishing you were dead since these symptoms began?
Patient: No, I don’t have thoughts of harming myself or wishing I was dead. I mostly just feel detached and apathetic, and I end up saying or doing things without much self-checking.
Doctor: Have you noticed any changes in your energy level—feeling unusually fatigued or sluggish throughout the day, even after rest?
Patient: I’d say I feel pretty sluggish and low-energy most days, and even when I rest it doesn’t really lift. I’m mostly indifferent to what’s going on around me.

Doctor: Have you had any recent changes in your medical health, new medications, or symptoms such as feeling unusually cold, constipation, dry skin, or hair loss that might suggest a thyroid or other endocrine issue?

Patient: I haven’t noticed anything like constipation, feeling unusually cold, dry skin, or hair loss. I don’t really keep track of medical changes; I just feel detached and indifferent, and my attention wanders.

Doctor: Over the past six months, have you noticed any changes in your ability to work, study, or maintain relationships—such as withdrawing from friends or family, or having trouble keeping up with responsibilities?

Patient: My relationships feel less important to me, especially with family—I don’t really withdraw on purpose, I just don’t stay engaged. Responsibilities have become harder because I’m slower to decide and I don’t really check myself before I act.
Doctor: Have you ever experienced periods where you felt unusually upbeat, had a lot of energy, needed very little sleep, or were more talkative and impulsive than usual?

Patient: I don’t think so—my mood has mostly been flat and numb, and I haven’t had times where I felt unusually energized or needed very little sleep. If I’m impulsive, it’s more like I say or do things without checking myself, not like I feel “up.”
